cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and the declaration is being made in the present.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: Let two or three things be true about what's arriving, then pick one and act on it today.
cells.core:
You can feel what's entering, and you don't have to make it single before you move. Several things can be true at once here: this is work, it's a relationship, it's a chance you didn't ask for. You can hold them all and still put your hand on one, and the one you choose is not a lie about the others.
This tends to look like speaking the true thing and watching it hold up. The same ability is working now: you're letting the arrival stay complicated and choosing anyway. Say what you actually see first, then take one step that only fits if it's true. You'll know more by lunch.

cells.tense: You will have already organized what is entering before it has arrived to be met.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Take one thing arriving and follow it all the way in until you hit its edge, then stop.
cells.core:
You're writing the ending before the scene starts. What's entering gets a full structure thrown around it, and the structure is going up faster than the thing itself. From where you sit that's just being ready. From the doorway it looks like nothing gets to arrive on terms other than yours.
Holding less won't help. Go further into one thing instead, until it shows you its limit. Pick the part that won't resolve and think it through past where it's comfortable, deeper than you'd take it by habit. Where the thinking can't continue, stop there. You'll learn the difference between planning and meeting.

cells.tense: You were standing at the door when it opened, and you are still standing there.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Pick the long build this arrival belongs to, and do today's small part of it once.
cells.core:
What was entering came in already. You can describe it clearly, and your hand hasn't moved toward it. You can organize a thing in your sleep, and none of that is being spent here. The waiting has its own shape now, and it looks like readiness. Going well, this is steady work: the thing you've built keeps its shape, and whoever leans on it finds it holds.
This is not a call to feel more. It's a call to build. Choose the longer thing this belongs to and do one small piece of it today, whether or not you feel assembled. Mastery comes from the days, not the mood. The door is behind you; the work is in front.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where you are already writing the structure.
cells.ask: Name three things this arrival has already grown in you, and keep them somewhere you'll see.
cells.core:
Something has been taking shape through you, and your account has it forming without your hand in it. Going well, this is gathering: you collect what a change yielded and know it was yours to collect. What's appearing now came from your building, and you talk as if you found it assembled.
Before you could organize anything, you collected what came of things. Pick up what this arrival has already grown — the instincts that got sharper, the thing you now know without arguing — and count it. Writing it down puts your name back on it. You waited out this yield, and the gathering is yours.
